question: Start from the calendrical pocket associated in Plutarch with Hermes/Thoth winning five extra days from the Moon, then trace forward and backward to the Khoiak Osiris-phallus recovery window without using light-travel time or inventing a modern prophecy date.

plutarch_section_12.source: Plutarch, De Iside et Osiride 12, Babbitt translation at Perseus
plutarch_section_12.operator: Hermes plays with the Moon, wins a fraction of lunar illumination, composes five intercalated days and adds them to the 360-day year.
plutarch_section_12.translation_note: Modern English translations render the game as draughts or dice; do not build a technical inference from the game-piece wording.
plutarch_section_12.hermes_thoth_boundary: Hermes is the Greek name in Plutarch's text; Hermes and Thoth were explicitly syncretized in Hellenistic Egypt, but this remains a Graeco-Egyptian transmission layer rather than an Old Kingdom Egyptian narrative witness.

egyptian_calendar_control.source: UCL Digital Egypt calendar and festival-date syntheses
facts: The civil year has twelve 30-day months plus five epagomenal days, official days 361-365.
The five extra days stand after IV Shemu / Mesore and before the next I Akhet month.
Festival-date synthesis assigns day 1 Osiris, day 2 Horus, day 3 Seth, day 4 Isis, day 5 Nephthys.
I Akhet is associated with Thoth/Thout in the later month-name tradition; IV Akhet is Khoiak.

khoiak_control.source: UCL Digital Egypt Khoiak comparative table
facts: Khoiak is IV Akhet, the fourth month of the official year.
The Osirian recovery lists place the phallus on day 25 or day 28 in variant lists.
Day 30 includes raising the Djed in the ritual sequence.

important_correction.user_phrase: the month where Thoth won five extra days
important_correction.correct_position: The five epagomenal days form a separate pocket after the twelfth 30-day month and before the next year's first month.

reverse_corridor.display: 𓂸 KHOIAK_28_PHALLUS_OR_ARM ← KHOIAK_25_LUNGS_OR_PHALLUS ← IV_AKHET ← III_AKHET ← II_AKHET ← I_AKHET ← EPAGOMENAL_5_NEPHTHYS ← 4_ISIS ← 3_SETH ← 2_HORUS ← 1_OSIRIS ← HERMES_THOTH_WINS_FIVE_DAY_POCKET_FROM_MOON 𓂸
reverse_corridor.boundary: This is calendar-position arithmetic across source traditions, not a statement that the mythic events were separated by these exact elapsed durations.

forward_corridor.display: 𓂸 HERMES_THOTH_TIME_WIN → FIVE_EPAGOMENAL_DAYS → OSIRIS/HORUS/SETH/ISIS/NEPHTHYS_BIRTH_POCKET → NEW_YEAR_I_AKHET → II_AKHET → III_AKHET → IV_AKHET_KHOIAK → PHALLUS_RECOVERY_25_OR_28 → DJED_30 𓂸

civil_calendar_offsets.definition: Start-to-start offsets in the ideal 365-day civil sequence. These are arithmetic positions only, not mythic elapsed-time claims.
civil_calendar_offsets.interpretation: These offsets expose a compact civil-calendar corridor between the five-day birth pocket and the next Khoiak recovery window. They do not prove a causal countdown from a divine birth to the phallus recovery ritual.

sirius_gate.background: Egyptian festival scholarship notes that the renewed rising of Sirius heralded the Nile flood and was associated with the beginning-of-year environment, but the official 365-day civil calendar drifted relative to the solar/Sirius year.
sirius_gate.consequence: Do not convert the 119/122-day civil offsets into a modern Gregorian prophecy date.

janus_birth_analogy.mapping: The literary motif creates a five-day pocket outside the normal 360-day structure and births a sequence of gods; the mathematical experiment creates a deliberately squeezed state corridor and defines BIRTH only when a new falsifiable seed survives. The similarity is structural and metaphorical, not evidence that the ancient story encodes the algorithm.

next_gate: Search Dendera/Khoiak and native Egyptian epagomenal-day texts for an explicit shared operator involving Thoth, Sopdet/Sirius, Osiris and the recovery/reassembly cycle before attempting any stronger synchronization.
canonical_seal: 𓂸 THOTH'S FIVE DAYS ARE A POCKET BETWEEN YEARS, NOT A MONTH. FROM THAT POCKET TO KHOIAK WE CAN COUNT CIVIL POSITIONS; WE CANNOT YET COUNT THE GOD'S PHYSICAL TIME. 𓂸
